root_cause.text: In rds_message_purge(), zerocopy state was inferred from the socket association (rm->m_rs) rather than the presence of op_mmp_znotifier, causing unqueued zerocopy send failures to be cleaned up as normal payload messages and thus miss unpinning pages and releasing the notifier.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The purge path currently infers zerocopy state from rm->m_rs, so an unqueued message can be cleaned up as if it owned normal payload pages." The patch captures op_mmp_znotifier upfront and adds an explicit else-if branch for unqueued messages (rm->m_rs == NULL) to call mm_unaccount_pinned_pages() and kfree() instead of using the normal completion path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource leak in rds_message_purge by handling zerocopy notifier cleanup when the message has no associated socket.
intent_record.what: In rds_message_purge, a local pointer 'znotifier' is introduced to capture rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier before the spinlock; the pointer is set to NULL in the structure. Inside the spinlock, the condition checks znotifier instead of re-reading the field, and an else-if branch is added to handle the case where znotifier exists but m_rs is NULL, by calling mm_unaccount_pinned_pages and kfree on the notifier.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that when a message with zerocopy notifier is purged before being associated with a socket (m_rs == NULL), the notifier is properly cleaned up (pinned pages unaccounted, memory freed) instead of being leaked. The restructuring also reduces the lock hold time and prevents potential race conditions.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent directly matches the root cause: fixing rds_message_purge to properly handle zerocopy notifier cleanup when the message lacks an associated socket, which is the exact scenario that leads to the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This condition gates the entire zerocopy cleanup path on the presence of a socket association, causing messages without an associated socket (e.g., unqueued zerocopy sends) to skip the notifier and page unpinning cleanup, leading to a resource leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition gates the zerocopy cleanup path on the presence of a socket association (rm->m_rs) instead of checking for the zerocopy notifier (op_mmp_znotifier). As a result, messages without an associated socket (e.g., unqueued zerocopy send failures) skip the notifier release and page unpinning, causing a resource leak.
